items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Claude Beno Kennedy in their own turns; the name is introduced solely by the interviewer as someone the interviewee might have heard talk of.

ctx.x: I don't think it would be too bad. He lived and put in all my life. He might have drank once in a while. But he liked the ladies down there especially in the office in those times.

But Lazy Daddy was a very, very lovable fellow. He always had a pleasant word for everyone. I can't recall seeing him mad with anyone. And the trumpet player that left Troy's band that I succeeded in was one of the finest trumpet men I have ever heard and that's saying a lot. That was Claude Beno Kennedy. You've heard talk of him. He didn't last long enough to really imprint his name but he was a terrific trumpet player. And he joined Lazy Daddy's band to show Troy up, Troy Floyd's band, and come here doing it.…

Yeah they had a terrific band. And Henry stayed there in Houston for years. Henry was the type of musician that it was, it's amazing how he could do it. He couldn't read. And those shows would come in there. Well those shows would come down from Chicago and New York. Houston used to be a great theatrical town for Vaudeville and stuff like that. So they played a lot of them and I played them too. And we'd always like to get Henry because Henry could play that show down. Well you mean Lazy Daddy. Yeah.
